questions.q: What does this course assume you already know, and what does it do with that knowledge?
options: It assumes T-SQL Development's writing-SQL skills (queries, joins, procedures, schema design) and redirects them toward administration, security, performance, automation, and troubleshooting instead of re-teaching SQL syntax
It assumes no prior SQL knowledge at all and starts from SELECT statements
It assumes prior Azure experience but no SQL knowledge
It re-teaches every T-SQL concept from scratch before moving to administration topics
questions.explain: Every skill from T-SQL Development gets reused immediately, redirected toward a different job: keeping the database running, not writing more queries against it.

questions.q: What is the real difference between a developer's SQL knowledge and a DBA's job, per this lesson?
options: A developer's knowledge answers "how do I get the data I need?"; a DBA's job starts after that query already works — speed, access, and recoverability
There is no real difference — they are the same skill set
A DBA never needs to understand SQL queries at all
A developer's job is harder than a DBA's job in every case
questions.explain: This course is organized around exactly the DBA-side questions: performance, security, and disaster recovery, not more query syntax.

questions.q: Why do this course's chapter lengths deliberately differ instead of being split evenly?
options: They mirror the real DP-300 certification's domain weighting — e.g. Chapter 8 (Query Performance Tuning) gets 9 lessons because monitoring/performance is 20-25% of the real exam
Chapter lengths were chosen completely at random
Every chapter in this course actually has the exact same number of lessons
Longer chapters always cover easier material
questions.explain: Security and HA/DR similarly get more space because they're each 20-25% of the real DP-300 blueprint.

questions.q: What two topics does this course fold into Chapter 3 specifically because Microsoft added them to DP-300's current exam objectives?
options: Azure Arc-enabled SQL services and Azure SQL Database in Microsoft Fabric
Always On Availability Groups and Failover Cluster Instances
SQL Server Agent jobs and PowerShell scripting
Dynamic data masking and row-level security
questions.explain: These are newer additions to the real exam blueprint that this course deliberately does not skip.

questions.q: According to the chapter-by-chapter arc in this lesson, what comes right after the course establishes a working environment and the right deployment shape (Chapters 1-3)?
options: Locking the environment down — who can access what, over what network, with what encrypted (Chapters 4-6)
Immediately jumping to the final certification exam review
Migrating a production database, before any security work is done
Building the real-world capstone project first
questions.explain: Security comes before monitoring/performance, automation, migration, backup, and HA/DR in this course's deliberate ordering.
